title: A Song Is Born revisited: talent unused
summary: On Tape 11 he repeats that they had more talent than anyone in the film but were picked for a small part with little singing.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Mr. Bubbles, yesterday we were talking about "A Song is Born" with Danny Kaye and you mentioned to me that you felt that your talent wasn't utilized very well in that film. As a matter of fact you felt Buck and Bubbles was the strongest act in the film.
It wasn't acts, the idea is we felt we had more talent than any of the characters in the play.
What kind of roles did you play?
Window washers, like janitors -- but/ we were window washers.
Why would you choose such a role?
I didn't choose that, they picked us out for the part. We didn't pick the part. They picked us out for the part and that's the only thing they could find.
But yet you were noted for singing and dancing. Why didn't they have you do that in the show?

Don't ask me. I wouldn't know that. I didn't ask the producer, why can't I dance or why can't we tell jokes, I didn't ask him that. They got the part picked out for us to do and we just went and did the part that they had for us to do. That's more logical than anybody.
Was there any singing and dancing in the film at all?
Danny Kaye. And he had a girl -- can't think of her name -- but anyway less singing from Buck and Bubbles and less dancing from Buck and Bubbles.
